NFL.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than the Vegas favorite, it has mostly lost so far.
NFL.evidence: 2 of 7 graded games where the model's side was not the Vegas favorite won (CIN over BAL and DEN over KC won; PHI over DAL, NYG over NO, ATL over CHI, PHI over CAR, NE over CHI lost). No game on this week's lists disagrees with the Vegas favorite, so no new cases from these games.
NFL.test: On past seasons, take every game where the model's pick differs from the moneyline favorite. Compare its win rate and spread record with Vegas. Wait for 20+ games.

NFL.lesson: Large gaps between the model's total and Vegas's total have not paid off.
NFL.evidence: 0 of 5 graded games with a gap of 4.9 or more won the over/under pick. Gaps near 4 are mixed: ARI-DAL at 4.2 lost, JAX-BAL at 4.2 won, BUF-BAL at 3.9 won, CHI-SEA at 3.2 lost, TEN-CIN at 2.5 lost. Overall the over/under is 21-20. This week's TB-CHI Under (gap 5.0) and ARI-SEA Over (gap 4.9) add to the large-gap sample; news on ARI-SEA (backup QB with a sore elbow) does not favor the Over.
NFL.test: On past seasons, group games by size of the total gap (under 2, 2-4, over 4). Check hit rate per group. Needs 20+ games in the large-gap group.

NFL.lesson: Many big misses come from efficiency swings, which the model can't see before kickoff.
NFL.evidence: In 9 of the 15 games where the winner was wrong, the review names efficiency as the main reason (DAL-PHI, TB-CAR, NYG-HOU, ARI-LA, CHI-ATL, CAR-PHI, BAL-CLE, ARI-DAL, CHI-SEA). Turnovers led in NO-NYG and SF-ATL. Recent blowouts JAX-IND and PIT-CLE came from finishing drives, and JAX-BAL (17.5 off) from turnovers plus unexplained factors.
NFL.test: On past seasons, measure how often big spread misses (over 8 points) are driven by efficiency versus turnovers. Check whether the model's misses are larger than Vegas's overall.

NFL.lesson: Long-shot picks (underdog winners and big-game props) hit a bit below the model's chances and lose units.
NFL.evidence: Underdog picks are 4 of 14 against 5.5 expected (-3.96 units). Big-game picks are 8 of 27 against 8.9 expected (-9.46 units). Combined, 12 of 41 against 14.4 expected, so about 2 hits short, with the unit loss driven by prices. Milestone picks are 22 of 29 against 21.7 expected (-3.28 units).
NFL.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual hit rate for underdog winners and long-shot props in buckets of model chance. Also check whether the prices paid are shorter than fair odds. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

NFL.lesson: Best-value picks against the sportsbook are running below the model's chances.
NFL.evidence: 7 of 17 best-value picks hit this season, against 9.0 expected, at -3.64 units. All five this week sit only 0.0 to 2.0 points over break-even.
NFL.test: On past seasons, check hit rate of the model's top value picks by size of edge. Needs 20+ picks.

NFL.lesson: The model's margin errors are larger than Vegas's, and it is below .500 against the spread.
NFL.evidence: Average spread miss is 10.3 for the model against 9.4 for Vegas over 41 graded games. The model is 18-23-1 against the spread. Winners are 26 of 41.
NFL.test: On past seasons, compare the model's average absolute margin error with Vegas's, by week, over a full season. Also check ATS record by season. Do this before changing anything.

NFL.lesson: Big gaps between the model and Vegas may come from lineup changes the model hasn't picked up.
NFL.evidence: DAL at PHI listed Hurts, who was on IR, and DAL won 38-21 against the model's PHI by 3.9. PHI at WAS listed him again, and WAS won 27-10 against the model's WAS by 3.3 (Vegas -6). This week the brief lists Kyler Murray for MIN, but he is out and Carson Wentz starts. The model has MIN at 46% against Vegas 39%. The model also has DAL only 1.4 ahead at IND against Vegas -4.5, but DAL is missing Pick…
NFL.test: On past seasons, flag games where a starting QB differed from the one in the model's inputs. Compare the model's margin error in those games with all others. Needs 20+ such games.

NFL.lesson: Most-likely-winner picks have fallen short of the model's own chances.
NFL.evidence: 10 of 18 most-likely-winner picks hit this season, against 13.2 expected, at -5.31 units. Overall winners are 26 of 41 (63%). The sample is under 20 picks, so it stays at watching.
NFL.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (70-79%, 80%+) and compare hit rate with the moneyline-implied chance. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

College.lesson: The 'model total 3+ above Vegas means the over hits' pattern does not hold up; the over hit less often than not.
College.evidence: Weeks 8-9: over hit in 11 of 29 such games. Week 10 so far: 3 of 6 (James Madison, Ball State and Buffalo went over; New Mexico, Toledo and Ohio did not). Combined 14 of 35 (40%).
College.test: On past seasons, group games by model total minus Vegas total (0-3, 3-6, 6+) and check how often the over hits in each group. Need 20+ games per group.

College.lesson: Big misses are spread across several causes; efficiency leads less clearly than before.
College.evidence: Week 9 reviews, 26 games missed by 8+ points: efficiency first in 7, defensive/return touchdowns 6, turnovers 5, finishing drives 5, nothing stood out 3. Week 8 had efficiency first in 15 of 25. No new reviews this run. Efficiency is measured after the game, so it partly restates the miss.
College.test: On past seasons, check whether a team's success rate in prior games predicts the model's error next game. Also compare turnover margin, defensive/return touchdowns and points per trip inside the 40 with long-run averages, to see if misses lean one way or are random.

College.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than Vegas, results are mixed to poor.
College.evidence: About 4 of 11 right overall. No new disagreements among the 12 Week 10 results; the model and Vegas picked the same side in each. Ole Miss (model 50%, Vegas picks Georgia) is the open case this week. Sample is small.
College.test: On past seasons, list games where the model and Vegas disagree on the winner, then compare the model's win rate with Vegas's. Need 20+ games.

College.lesson: The 'Best value against the sportsbook' list has been weak.
College.evidence: Season: 8 of 22 hit against 11.2 expected, at -6.73 units. The edges are thin (about 51% against 52.4% needed), so the model's own chance is below break-even on all five Week 10 picks. Charlotte +8.5 points against the model's own UAB by 17.8.
College.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's spread and total picks by edge size and compare hit rates with the 52.4% break-even. Check that each pick's cover chance matches the model's own margin. Need 20+ games per bucket.

College.lesson: Underdog picks have hit a bit less often than the model expected, but long prices have kept units positive.
College.evidence: Season: 7 of 22 hit against 8.3 expected, at +0.48 units (was 6 of 21, 7.9 expected, -1.16 units last run). One more hit swung the units a lot, which shows how much luck is in this list.
College.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual win rate for the model's underdog picks, in buckets of model chance (under 35%, 35-45%, 45%+). Need 20+ picks per bucket.

College.lesson: The 'Most likely winners' list has landed close to the model's own chances.
College.evidence: Season: 17 of 19 hit against 17.0 expected, at -0.30 units. Prices are very short, so one miss costs a lot. Only 19 picks.
College.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (90%+, 85-90%) and compare with actual win rate and with Vegas's no-vig chance. Need 20+ games per bucket.

College.lesson: The model's spread misses are slightly larger than Vegas's over the season.
College.evidence: Season (184 games): average spread miss 12.3 points for the model against 11.7 for Vegas, a 0.6 gap unchanged. Winners right in 122 of 184 (66%), spread record 88-89-4. Week 10 so far: 6 of 12 winners and 6-5-1 against the spread.
College.test: On past seasons, compare the model's and Vegas's average spread error. Then test whether averaging the model's margin and Vegas's margin beats either alone, and whether the gap changes by week of season.

College.lesson: The model does not see starting-quarterback injuries; when a QB is out, its margin runs well above Vegas's.
College.evidence: Week 9: Kansas State (starter and backup hurt) was model +9.1 vs Vegas +2.5 and lost 27-24 at Colorado. This week Boise State's Madsen is out (model Boise State by 24.5 vs Vegas 16.5), Florida switches QBs, and Air Force's QB is questionable. One graded game so far; the Boise State result will be the second.
College.test: On past seasons, flag games where a team's starting QB was out and compare the model's margin error and the Vegas error in those games with all other games. Need 20+ such games.
